newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* Dow Jones closed on Wednesday at 5,930.62 points, down 36.15
* Nikkei average closed at 20,870.83 points, down 167.70. The Tokyo stock market is closed on Thursday for a holiday.
* Hang Seng closed at 12,250.57 points, up 143.81
* The Philippine Stock Exchange index closed on Wednesday at 3,026.24 points, down 11.30.
* The peso closed unchanged at 26.269 to a U.S. dollar.
* Interbank call loan rate fell to 12.59375 pct vs 12.75
pct
* Manila shares are expected to drift slightly down on Thursday with foreign investors continuing to sell, though at a decelarated pace, brokers said.

* Brokerage Angping Securities said Bank of the Philippine Islands, expected to make a secondary offering of shares worth around two billion to five billion pesos, would provide more liquidity to the stock.
Angping quoted BPI officials as saying there were shareholders willing to sell their stake after the bank issued some 1.158 billion pesos worth of common shares in exchange for Citytrust shares.

* Angping Securities said it expected "things can start getting better for Mondragon International". The Securities and Exchange Commission had lifted the cease and desist order against the sale by Mondragon Leisure and Resorts Corp of club membership shares and playing rights, it said.

* A Reuter poll on Wednesday predicted PLDT's first nine months net profits would reach 4.53 billion pesos. In the first nine months last year, PLDT's profits were 4.6 billion pesos but that figure was boosted by an extraordinary income of 1.154 billion pesos.
* Megaworld Properties & Holdings said on Wednesday it is planning to raise 3.5 billion pesos from a preferred share offering to fund its various acitivities.

* Brokerage Sun Hung Kai said in a report it expected a technical rebound within the next few days as index heavyweights, at this point, remain oversold. "From here, we may see some repositioning as investors prepare for announcement of third quarter 1996 earnings," it said.
* Brokerage BPI Securities said it saw support for the market at the 3,000 level. The decline in prices has decelerated and the volume trade for Wednesday decreased to 2.1 billion pesos.
BPI Securities said it saw the drop in prices and the consolidation process to continue for the short term.
* Marshall Mays, regional strategist at Nikko Research Centre (Hong Kong) Ltd told Reuters on Wednesday that foreign fund selling in the Philippines in the past few days was part of profit-taking.
Mays added: "Foreigners have been the main sellers in the Philippines, but the liquidity is still there...I think Manila will be back up to 32 or 33 by the end of the year."
